subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
subtype: Approach: rehearsing the presentation to judges [Action]
passage:
Tuesday, 8 pm.
Practised our three-minute talk today in front of Thomas Sir and two parents. I talked too fast and used words like differential steering without explaining. Mrs Shah asked, “What does that mean?” and I froze. Thomas Sir said, “Good. That is exactly the question the judges will ask.” So I rewrote that part using a picture of a shopping trolley. Second time through, everyone nodded. We also listed likely questions: How much did it cost? (about 3,200 rupees) Is it safe near other people? (battery cut-off switch, no exposed wires). I wrote both answers on a card. Amma says her boy talks too fast when nervous, so I'm slowing down. Time: 2 min 50 sec.
— Zubin

qa.q: How long did the final version of the talk take?
What did Zubin feel when Mrs Shah asked what differential steering means?
qa.a: Zubin felt nervous and put on the spot, since he froze.

qa.q: What else could Zubin do before the judges?
qa.a: Zubin could practise with someone outside the team, since a new listener shows which parts are still unclear.

qa.q: How might Mrs Shah see the improved talk?
qa.a: Mrs Shah probably understands it much better, since she asked because the term was unclear and then saw everyone nod.

grounding: Students practise explaining their design in three minutes to a teacher and parents, refine unclear parts after questions and prepare answers about cost and safety.
